rules.title: Entity has no permission decorator
rules.summary: Every entity declares `@authenticated`, `@anonymous`, or `@role` explicitly
rules.why: An entity without a permission decorator isn't locked down — it silently gets `authenticated: *`, so every signed-in user can create, read, update, and delete every row.
rules.fix: Add an explicit decorator: `@authenticated('*', { policy: (claims, item) => claims.sub.eq(item.user_id) })` for per-user data, or `@authenticated('read')` for shared reference data.

rules.title: Protected page is reachable without signing in
rules.summary: Pages that use app data wait for the session and require sign-in
rules.why: Without a guard, signed-out visitors can open pages that call the data API — the calls fail or show UI meant for signed-in users — and apps that never wire up sign-in can't load authenticated data at all.
rules.fix: Wrap protected routes in a guard that waits for the auth context's `loading` state and redirects to the sign-in page when `!isAuthenticated`, and make sure the auth provider is set up before any data call.
rules.check: Read the frontend's entry point, app component (or router config) and pages: src/main.tsx and src/App.tsx, or the same files under the frontend package's src/ when rayfin.yml's services.staticHosting.path names one (such as packages/frontend/src). Flag routes or pages that call client.data (directly or through services) but render without a guard that checks isAuthenticated/loading from the auth context. Also flag an app whose data calls run while its auth provider/bootstrap is never wired (for example, auth scaffolding left commented out). Don't flag genuinely public pages that use no Rayfin data.

rules.title: `onAuthStateChange` doesn't exist in Rayfin
rules.summary: Session changes are observed with `onSessionChange`
rules.why: The Rayfin auth client has no `onAuthStateChange` (a name from other auth SDKs), so code that calls it throws at runtime.
rules.fix: Subscribe with `client.auth.onSessionChange(callback)`, which returns an unsubscribe function.

rules.title: Fabric SSO is enabled but its provider package isn't installed
rules.summary: Apps with Fabric SSO depend on `@microsoft/rayfin-auth-provider-fabric`
rules.why: `services.auth.fabric.enabled` turns on the backend flow, but the frontend needs `@microsoft/rayfin-auth-provider-fabric` to actually sign users in.
rules.fix: Install `@microsoft/rayfin-auth-provider-fabric` at the same version as the rest of the Rayfin SDK and sign in with `ensureSignedInWithFabric`.

rules.title: Fabric auth provider is only imported lazily
rules.summary: The Fabric auth provider is imported statically at startup
rules.why: The provider captures the `?fabricEmbedded=true` flag when its module first loads. Loading it only through `import()` can miss the flag, so sign-in inside Fabric falls back to a popup.
rules.fix: Import `@microsoft/rayfin-auth-provider-fabric` statically from the app's entry module (or a module it imports at startup).

docs.title: Embedded flow: automatic sign-in on startup

rules.title: Popup sign-in starts without a user click
rules.summary: Popup sign-in is started directly from a user gesture
rules.why: `ensureSignedInWithFabric` ends by calling `window.open()`, which browsers block unless it runs directly inside a click — so sign-in silently fails.
rules.fix: Call it from a button's `onClick` before any `await`. For automatic sign-in on page load inside Fabric, use `initEmbeddedAuth()` instead, which never opens a popup.
rules.check: Find calls to ensureSignedInWithFabric or initiateFabricLogin (and wrappers that call them, such as a signIn method). Flag calls made from useEffect, on module load, on a timer, or after an await rather than directly in a click handler. initEmbeddedAuth on startup is correct and must not be flagged.

docs.title: Popup flow: sign in from a button

rules.title: Mock sign-in with hard-coded credentials ships in the app
rules.summary: No mock sign-in with hard-coded credentials is part of the app
rules.why: A leftover `MockAuthService` signs in with a fixed email and password through a local-backend flow that Fabric apps don't support, and it can take over when configuration is missing.
rules.fix: Delete `MockAuthService` and the local-dev branch that selects it, or replace it with an in-memory test double that only tests import.

rules.title: Entra token sign-in isn't enabled in rayfin.yml
rules.summary: Apps that sign in with an Entra token, including local automatic sign-in, enable `externalEntraExchange`
rules.why: `signInWithEntraToken()` and local automatic sign-in (`fetchRayfinLocalSessionToken()`) exchange a delegated Entra token for a Rayfin session. Unless `services.auth.fabric.externalEntraExchange` is `true`, the backend rejects it with "External Entra exchange is not enabled."
rules.fix: Set `externalEntraExchange: true` under `services.auth.fabric` in rayfin.yml.

rules.title: Code depends on undocumented session fields
rules.summary: Only documented session fields are read
rules.why: Rayfin sessions are intentionally opaque. Code that reads or decodes anything beyond `user`, `isAuthenticated`, `isAnonymous`, `role`, and `expiresAt` breaks when the SDK changes the session shape.
rules.fix: Gate UI on `session.isAuthenticated` or `session.user`, and use only the documented fields.
rules.check: Look at code that handles client.auth.getSession() or onSessionChange results. Flag reads of properties other than user, isAuthenticated, isAnonymous, role and expiresAt, or any decoding of tokens taken from the session.

rules.title: Signed-in UI renders before embedded sign-in finishes
rules.summary: Startup waits for `initEmbeddedAuth()` before showing signed-in UI or loading data
rules.why: Inside Fabric, `initEmbeddedAuth()` signs the user in and, since Rayfin 1.36, first checks for an external embed host. Rendering signed-in UI or calling the data API before it resolves can use a stale session from another user, or no session at all.
rules.fix: Await `initEmbeddedAuth()` in the auth provider before setting `loading` to false, and gate data calls and protected routes on that state.
rules.check: Read the auth provider and startup code (for example src/hooks/AuthContext.tsx, src/main.tsx, src/services/*Auth*). Confirm initEmbeddedAuth() (or a wrapper around it) is awaited before initial loading completes and before any client.data call or authenticated route renders. Flag startup code that shows authenticated UI or calls client.data while it is still pending, or a Fabric SSO app that never calls initEmbeddedAuth on startup.

rules.title: Per-user data isn't restricted to its owner
rules.summary: Entities with an owner field only let owners change their rows
rules.why: The entity stores an owner (`user_id`, `owner_id`, `created_by`, …) but a signed-in grant that can create, update, or delete has no row-level `policy` — so any signed-in user can change everyone's rows.
rules.fix: Add `policy: (claims, item) => claims.sub.eq(item.user_id)` to each grant that should be owner-scoped. Use separate decorators per action when reads are shared but writes aren't.

rules.title: Anyone can change this data without signing in
rules.summary: Anonymous (public) grants are read-only
rules.why: An `@anonymous` grant that includes create, update, or delete lets unauthenticated callers modify rows.
rules.fix: Limit `@anonymous` to `'read'` for genuinely public data, and move writes to `@authenticated` with an owner policy.

rules.title: Anonymous data access may be rejected on Fabric
rules.summary: Public (anonymous) data access is only used where the tenant allows it
rules.why: Anonymous data access on Fabric requires a tenant admin to enable it, and the CLI currently rejects configurations that grant the `anonymous` role at apply time — so the deploy or schema apply can fail.
rules.fix: Use `@authenticated('read')` for data only signed-in users need. Keep `@anonymous('read')` only for genuinely public data, and confirm your tenant allows anonymous data access.

rules.title: Policy uses an unsupported claim
rules.summary: Policies only compare `claims.sub`, `claims.email`, or `claims.role`
rules.why: The policy DSL supports only `sub`, `email`, and `role`. Other claims (tenant, organization, custom) don't compile or never match.
rules.fix: Store the value on the row (for example `organization_id`) and scope with `claims.sub` plus a membership check in application code.

rules.title: Storage folder has no permission decorator
rules.summary: Every `@blob()` storage class declares explicit permissions
rules.why: Storage folders are secured with the same `@authenticated` / `@anonymous` / `@role` decorators as entities; without one, who can read and write files isn't explicit.
rules.fix: Add a decorator such as `@authenticated('*', { policy: (claims, item) => claims.sub.eq(item.owner_id) })` to the `@blob()` class.

rules.title: Use the `@authenticated` / `@anonymous` shorthand
rules.summary: Built-in roles use the `@authenticated` / `@anonymous` shorthands
rules.why: `@role('authenticated', …)` works, but the shorthands are the documented style and make intent clearer at the call site.
rules.fix: Replace `@role('authenticated', …)` with `@authenticated(…)` and `@role('anonymous', …)` with `@anonymous(…)`.

rules.title: Sensitive field is readable through the data API
rules.summary: Sensitive fields are excluded from read grants
rules.why: Fields such as secrets, tokens, passwords, or sensitive personal data are returned to every caller allowed to read the entity unless they are excluded.
rules.fix: Add `exclude: ['field']` to the read grant (use separate decorators per action if writes still need it), or move the value out of the entity to a server-side secret.
rules.check: In the data model's entities (rayfin/data/, or the data package's src/ when rayfin.yml's services.data.path names one, such as packages/data/src), find fields holding secrets, credentials, tokens, API keys, passwords or sensitive personal data (for example ssn, salary, date of birth). Flag them when a read grant for any role neither lists them in exclude nor omits them from include. Ordinary profile data such as display names isn't sensitive.

rules.title: Grant is broader than the data needs
rules.summary: Each role gets only the actions it needs
rules.why: Granting `'*'` (or update and delete) to every signed-in user on shared data lets any user edit or delete it, and unscoped reads of per-user data expose everyone's rows.
rules.fix: Split grants per action — for example `@authenticated('read')` for everyone and owner-scoped policies (or no grant) for writes.
rules.check: For each entity, compare its grants with how the frontend uses it. Flag '*' or write actions granted to all signed-in (or anonymous) users on shared or reference data, and reads of per-user private data granted without a policy. Skip entities the quick checks already reported.

rules.title: Row policy never checks who the caller is
rules.summary: Row policies on per-user data compare a claim
rules.why: A policy that only compares the row's own fields (never `claims`) filters rows but doesn't restrict them to the signed-in user.
rules.fix: Add a caller term such as `claims.sub.eq(item.user_id)`, combining it with `.and()` if the existing filter is still needed.
rules.check: Find policy callbacks whose body never uses the claims parameter. Flag them when the entity looks user-owned (an owner field, per-user UI), not when the filter is clearly intended for shared data.

rules.title: Team data isn't checked against membership
rules.summary: Team-scoped data checks membership before reads and writes
rules.why: Policies can't express "the caller belongs to `item.organization_id`", so without a membership check in the app a user can read or write another team's rows.
rules.fix: Look up the caller's memberships first and filter reads by `organization_id`, and verify membership before creating or updating rows for an organization.
rules.check: If entities carry organization_id, team_id or workspace_id values shared across users, check that reads filter by the caller's memberships and that writes verify membership first, following the documented per-organization pattern. Flag missing checks.

rules.title: Per-user rules on a connector that runs as the app
rules.summary: Connectors whose data is scoped per user use delegated auth
rules.why: With `auth.type: application`, every connector query runs as the app's identity, so the source can't tell users apart and a policy comparing `claims.sub` or `claims.email` doesn't limit what each person sees there. Since Rayfin 1.36, `rayfin connector add` defaults SQL connectors to `application`.
rules.fix: Use `auth.type: delegated` for connectors whose data must be scoped to each user, or drop the per-user rules if everyone may see the data.
rules.check: In rayfin.yml, find connectors with auth.type: application. For their entities under rayfin/connectors/<name>/, and the app code that reads them, flag per-user policies (claims.sub / claims.email comparisons) or UI that assumes each signed-in user only sees their own rows. Don't flag shared reference data.

rules.title: Secret exposed through a browser-visible variable
rules.summary: Browser-visible variables (`VITE_`, `RAYFIN_PUBLIC_`) hold no secrets
rules.why: `VITE_*` and `RAYFIN_PUBLIC_*` values are compiled into the browser bundle, so anyone using the app can read them.
rules.fix: Remove the value from frontend variables, store it with `rayfin secret set <NAME>`, and read it server-side from a Rayfin function. If the key is designed to be public (for example a browser-restricted maps key), dismiss this as an accepted risk.

rules.title: Environment file isn't git-ignored
rules.summary: Local environment files are git-ignored
rules.why: `rayfin/.env` and `.env.local` hold deployment values and sometimes secrets. If they aren't ignored they end up in git history.
rules.fix: Add the file to `.gitignore`, commit a placeholder `.env.example` instead, and rotate anything that was already committed.

rules.title: Credential hard-coded in the project
rules.summary: No credentials are hard-coded in source, scripts, or workflows
rules.why: Keys, tokens, and connection strings in committed files are visible to anyone with the code and stay in git history even after you delete them.
rules.fix: Move the value to a Rayfin secret (`rayfin secret set`) or your CI secret store, reference it by name, and rotate the exposed credential.

rules.title: Redirect URIs allow unexpected origins
rules.summary: `allowedRedirectUris` lists only the app's own origins
rules.why: Every listed origin can receive the Fabric SSO hand-off. Wildcards and plain-`http` non-local origins widen who can receive it.
rules.fix: Keep only your local dev origin (such as `http://localhost:5173`) and the app's own deployed origin, and remove wildcards and entries copied from other projects.

rules.title: Publishable-key variable holds something else
rules.summary: Publishable-key variables contain a publishable key (`pk-…`)
rules.why: Only publishable keys (`pk-…`) are safe in client code. Any other value in this variable ships to the browser.
rules.fix: Restore the value that `rayfin up` / `rayfin env` generate (it starts with `pk-`), and rotate the value that was pasted by mistake.

rules.title: Deployment registry isn't git-ignored
rules.summary: `rayfin/.deployments.json` is git-ignored
rules.why: It holds workspace, tenant, and item IDs for your own deployments and is regenerated by `rayfin up`; it isn't meant to be shared.
rules.fix: Add `rayfin/.deployments.json` to `.gitignore` and untrack it with `git rm --cached rayfin/.deployments.json`.

rules.title: Plaintext token cache enabled in a committed file
rules.summary: Plaintext CLI token caching isn't enabled in committed files
rules.why: `RAYFIN_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK_ENABLED` stores the CLI token cache in plaintext and is meant for local development only.
rules.fix: Remove it from committed scripts, env files, and CI configuration; set it only in a local shell when you need it.

rules.title: Browser code calls a service with a secret credential
rules.summary: Credentials for other services stay server-side
rules.why: Anything the browser sends is visible to users, so calling paid or privileged APIs from frontend code exposes the credential.
rules.fix: Move the call into a Rayfin function that reads the key as `ctx.Secrets.<NAME>` (store it with `rayfin secret set`), and call that function from the app. Functions aren't available in every Fabric region, so confirm they deploy in your workspace.
rules.check: Look for frontend code that sends API keys, bearer tokens or other credentials to other services (fetch or axios headers, SDK constructors), or that embeds such values. Rayfin publishable keys (pk-…) and keys designed to be public are fine. Mask any value you quote.

rules.title: Text field has no maximum length
rules.summary: Every `@text` and `@email` field sets `max`
rules.why: On MSSQL, a `@text()` or `@email()` without `max` becomes `NVARCHAR(MAX)`, which can break GraphQL schema generation — the deploy reports success, then queries fail with an internal server error.
rules.fix: Set an explicit length, for example `@text({ max: 200 })`. Use `max: 128` for owner ids that come from `claims.sub`.

rules.title: Foreign key is typed as text
rules.summary: Foreign keys to other entities use `@uuid`
rules.why: A `{property}_id` column that references another entity must match that entity's UUID primary key; declaring it `@text()` is a type mismatch.
rules.fix: Declare it `@uuid()`. Owner ids derived from sign-in (like `user_id` from `claims.sub`) aren't foreign keys and stay `@text({ max: 128 })`.

rules.title: Relationship target isn't wrapped in an arrow function
rules.summary: `@one` / `@many` targets use a lazy arrow function
rules.why: `@one(Target)` evaluates the class immediately, which breaks on circular imports between entity files.
rules.fix: Write `@one(() => Target)` and `@many(() => Target)`.

rules.title: Entity import won't work at runtime
rules.summary: Entity files import related classes as values, with `.js` paths
rules.why: Relationship decorators need the runtime class, but `import type` is erased at compile time. Relative imports between entity files also need the `.js` extension to resolve as ESM.
rules.fix: Use `import { Target } from './Target.js'`.

rules.title: Entity isn't fully registered in the schema
rules.summary: Every entity is in both the `schema` array and the schema type
rules.why: An entity missing from the schema file (`schema.ts`, or a data package's `src/index.ts`) isn't part of the typed client (`client.data.<Entity>` won't exist), and one listed in only the array or only the type is half-registered.
rules.fix: Import it with a `.js` path and add it to both the exported schema type and the `schema` array.

rules.title: Entity property has no field decorator
rules.summary: Every entity property has exactly one field decorator
rules.why: Properties without a type decorator (`@text`, `@int`, `@uuid`, …) aren't stored, and two type decorators on one property conflict — reads and writes won't behave as the class suggests.
rules.fix: Give each stored property exactly one field decorator (for example `@int()`), and move values that shouldn't be stored out of the entity class.

rules.title: Decimal precision or scale is incomplete
rules.summary: `@decimal` sets precision and scale together, with precision ≤ 28
rules.why: Data API Builder supports a precision of at most 28, and setting only one of `precision` / `scale` gives an unexpected column type.
rules.fix: Set both, for example `@decimal({ precision: 18, scale: 2 })`.

rules.title: Optional field is only marked optional in one place
rules.summary: Nullable fields use `{ optional: true }` together with `?`
rules.why: Fields are required by default. `optional: true` without `?` (or `?` without the option) makes the database and the TypeScript type disagree.
rules.fix: Use both together, for example `@text({ optional: true, max: 200 }) note?: string`.

rules.title: Many-to-many relationship without a join entity
rules.summary: Many-to-many links go through an explicit join entity
rules.why: `@one` / `@many` only model one-to-many. Two entities pointing `@many` at each other doesn't create a working link.
rules.fix: Add a join entity with two `@one()` fields — one for each side — and query through it.

rules.title: Entity name is reserved by GraphQL
rules.summary: No entity is named after a built-in GraphQL type
rules.why: Entity names become GraphQL type names. Since Rayfin 1.36 the CLI rejects names such as `Date`, `String`, `Query`, or `UUID`, and anything starting with `__`, so the deploy stops.
rules.fix: Rename the class (for example `EventDate` instead of `Date`), or keep it and pass a safe name with `@entity('EventDate')`.

docs.title: Entity names can't reuse GraphQL built-in type names

rules.title: Relationship decorator has an unsupported option
rules.summary: `@one()` and `@many()` use only `optional` and `unique`
rules.why: Relationship decorators accept only `{ optional, unique }`. Options such as `default`, `max`, `foreignKey`, or `targetKey` aren't supported; the foreign key is always the `<property>_id` column.
rules.fix: Remove the other options and use the `<property>_id` foreign key the relationship generates.

rules.title: Field accepts values the app never uses
rules.summary: Fields use the tightest documented type and limits
rules.why: Free text for a fixed set of choices, text for emails, or unbounded numbers let invalid data bypass the UI and break filters, charts, and totals.
rules.fix: Use documented options: `@set([...])` for fixed choices, `@email()` for emails, and `min` / `max` on numbers and text.
rules.check: Compare entity fields with how the UI uses them. Flag fields where the UI offers a fixed set of values but the field is free @text, emails stored as @text, or numbers with obvious bounds but no min/max. Recommend only decorators and options that exist in the installed @microsoft/rayfin-core (check its type definitions or the field-types guide); for example, there is no index option.

rules.title: Seed script writes to a sign-in-only entity
rules.summary: Seed scripts only target entities that allow scripted writes
rules.why: There is no supported way to script data into entities that require sign-in, so these seed scripts fail.
rules.fix: Seed only `@anonymous()` entities from scripts, and create signed-in data through the running app.
rules.check: If the project has seed scripts (for example scripts/seed*.ts that use RayfinServerClient), flag writes to entities whose relevant action is only granted to signed-in users.

docs.title: No supported path for authenticated entities

rules.title: List query silently stops at 100 rows
rules.summary: Lists that can grow page through their results
rules.why: `.execute()` returns a single page — 100 rows by default — with no signal that more exist, so the app silently shows incomplete lists and totals as tables grow.
rules.fix: Use `.first(n).executePaginated()` and follow `.after(endCursor)` while `hasNextPage` is true, or load more pages on demand.
rules.check: Find client.data.<Entity> collection queries that end in .execute() (not findById) whose results are rendered as lists, used for totals or exports, or used in calculations, where the entity can plausibly exceed 100 rows and the query isn't bounded by a selective filter. Report the query location and mention where its result is used.

rules.title: `.count()` doesn't exist on Rayfin queries
rules.summary: Row counts use result length or a numeric aggregation
rules.why: The fluent client has no `count()` method. `count` is an aggregation over a numeric field that counts non-null values, not rows.
rules.fix: For a row count, select minimal fields and use `results.length` (summing pages for large tables), or aggregate `count` over a non-nullable numeric field.

rules.title: `findByPk` doesn't exist — use `findById`
rules.summary: Single-record reads use `findById`
rules.why: Rayfin has no `findByPk` (a name from other ORMs), so these calls fail.
rules.fix: Use `client.data.<Entity>.findById(id)`.

rules.title: Code relies on `totalCount`, which is never set
rules.summary: No code relies on `totalCount`
rules.why: Data API Builder can't return total counts, so `totalCount` exists on the result type but is never populated.
rules.fix: Count the loaded items instead, or page with `.executePaginated()` and sum `items.length`.

rules.title: Filter uses a relationship dot-path
rules.summary: Filters use foreign-key columns, not dot-paths
rules.why: Dot-paths such as `'notebook.id'` only work in `.select()`. In `.where()` they fail or filter nothing.
rules.fix: Filter by the foreign-key column: `.where({ notebook_id: { eq: notebookId } })`.

docs.title: Filter by foreign key, not by dot-path

rules.title: Select reaches more than one relationship deep
rules.summary: Selects use at most one relationship level
rules.why: `.select()` supports one level of relationship dot-path (`'notebook.name'`), not two (`'notebook.owner.email'`).
rules.fix: Run a second query for the deeper data, or add a direct relationship on the entity that needs it.

rules.title: Aggregation is combined with row selection
rules.summary: Aggregations aren't combined with `select` / `orderBy` / `first` / `after`
rules.why: Data API Builder rejects grouped aggregation together with row queries, so these chains fail.
rules.fix: Run the aggregation on its own, then sort or slice the returned groups in TypeScript.

rules.title: Sort direction isn't lowercase
rules.summary: `orderBy` uses `'asc'` / `'desc'`
rules.why: Sort directions are the lowercase strings `'asc'` and `'desc'`, not capitalized constants.
rules.fix: Write `.orderBy({ createdAt: 'desc' })`.

rules.title: Data is fetched with hand-built GraphQL
rules.summary: App data goes through the typed client (`client.data`)
rules.why: Hand-built `fetch()` or GraphQL calls to the Rayfin API skip the typed client's session handling and type safety.
rules.fix: Use `client.data.<Entity>` queries and mutations instead.

rules.title: One query per item in a loop
rules.summary: Related data is loaded in batches, not one query per row
rules.why: Awaiting a query for each list item multiplies round-trips — and capacity usage — as data grows.
rules.fix: Load everything in one query with `.where({ id: { in: ids } })`, a one-level `.select()` dot-path, or an aggregation.
rules.check: Find loops (for, for...of, map, forEach, or Promise.all over an array) that await a client.data call once per element.

rules.title: Mutation doesn't follow the documented shape
rules.summary: Mutations set relationships the documented way
rules.why: Setting a raw foreign-key column (`notebook_id`) in `create` / `update` isn't how relationships are written, and assigning arrays to `@many` fields does nothing.
rules.fix: Pass the related object instead — `notebook: { id: notebookId }` — and change a `@many` side by updating each child's `@one`.
rules.check: Review create, update and upsert calls against the installed rayfin-data types and the mutations guide. Flag raw {property}_id keys set where the entity declares a matching @one relationship, arrays written to @many properties, and update/delete calls targeting something other than the record id.

rules.title: rayfin.yml doesn't declare auth and data
rules.summary: rayfin.yml declares `services.auth` and `services.data`, even when disabled
rules.why: The CLI reads these keys without applying defaults, so leaving one out makes deploys fail.
rules.fix: Add both blocks — for example `data: { enabled: false }` when the app doesn't store data.

rules.title: Data service needs `dialect: mssql`
rules.summary: The data service declares `dialect: mssql`
rules.why: With `services.data.enabled: true`, `dialect` is required and Fabric apps support only `mssql` — otherwise the deploy fails with "Dialect is required when Data module is enabled".
rules.fix: Set `dialect: mssql` under `services.data`.

rules.title: Legacy decorators are enabled in tsconfig
rules.summary: tsconfig doesn't enable `experimentalDecorators` or `emitDecoratorMetadata`
rules.why: Rayfin uses standard TC39 decorators. The legacy `experimentalDecorators` mode (and `emitDecoratorMetadata`, which requires it) breaks entity compilation.
rules.fix: Remove `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` from every tsconfig.

rules.title: tsconfig is missing `ESNext.Decorators`
rules.summary: The tsconfig used for entities includes `ESNext.Decorators`
rules.why: The `ESNext.Decorators` library is what enables type-checking of Rayfin's standard decorators.
rules.fix: Add `"ESNext.Decorators"` to `compilerOptions.lib` in the root tsconfig.json.

rules.title: Build plugin can't compile the entity classes the app imports
rules.summary: Frontend code that imports entity classes builds with a decorator-capable plugin
rules.why: `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc` can't parse standard decorators. Importing entity classes as values (not `import type`) pulls them into the browser build, which then fails with "Expression expected".
rules.fix: Import entities with `import type`, or switch to `@vitejs/plugin-react`.

rules.title: Vite target is too old for the entity classes it bundles
rules.summary: Vite targets ES2022 or later when the bundle includes entity classes
rules.why: When the browser build includes decorated entity classes, esbuild must target ES2022 or later, or decorator syntax fails to parse.
rules.fix: Set `target: 'es2022'` under `build`, `esbuild`, and `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` in vite.config.ts.

rules.title: Static hosting folder doesn't match the build output
rules.summary: `staticHosting.folder` matches the frontend's build output directory
rules.why: `rayfin up` uploads `staticHosting.folder`. If it differs from where the bundler writes the build, the deploy fails or publishes stale files.
rules.fix: Make `services.staticHosting.folder` match Vite's `build.outDir` (default `dist`).

rules.title: rayfin.yml has deprecated keys
rules.summary: rayfin.yml uses no deprecated keys
rules.why: These keys are legacy or ignored: top-level `frontend:` (the framework is auto-detected) and `publishable_key:` (managed in `rayfin/.env`), `services.connectors.enabled` (connectors are always on since Rayfin 1.36), and `services.staticHosting.anonymousAccess` (replaced by `assetAccess` in 1.35.1).
rules.fix: Remove them from rayfin.yml. If you remove `anonymousAccess`, set `assetAccess` to `protected` or `public` instead.

rules.title: Connectors use the old map shape in rayfin.yml
rules.summary: `connectors:` in rayfin.yml is a list of entries
rules.why: Current Rayfin CLIs read `connectors:` as a list of `- name:` entries with a `type`; the older map keyed by connector name isn't the documented shape.
rules.fix: Rewrite each connector as a list item with `name` and `type` (for example by re-running `rayfin connector add`), keeping its `config`, `auth`, and `operations`.

rules.title: Functions are enabled without application auth
rules.summary: Enabled Functions declare `auth.type: application`
rules.why: Since Rayfin 1.36, `rayfin up` refuses to deploy enabled Functions unless `services.functions.auth.type` is `application`: "authentication is required when Functions are enabled."
rules.fix: Add `auth: { type: application }` under `services.functions` in rayfin.yml. Functions then call other services as the app's identity.

docs.title: Authentication is required when Functions are enabled

rules.title: Static hosting doesn't say who can load the app
rules.summary: `services.staticHosting.assetAccess` is set explicitly
rules.why: Since Rayfin 1.35.1 a hosted app must choose `protected` (Fabric sign-in required) or `public`. When it's missing, the first non-interactive deploy writes `protected` into rayfin.yml for you, so access isn't a deliberate choice.
rules.fix: Add `assetAccess: protected` under `services.staticHosting` (or `public` if anyone with the link should load the app's files; data permissions still apply).

rules.title: Embedded-only app is set to public
rules.summary: `assetAccess: public` isn't combined with `embedded.only: true`
rules.why: An app that only loads inside the Fabric portal has no standalone page to make public, so `rayfin up` rejects the combination with "Invalid static hosting posture".
rules.fix: Use `assetAccess: protected` for an embedded-only app, or set `embedded.only: false` if it should also load on its own.

rules.title: Feature flag turns on a capability that no longer needs one
rules.summary: `RAYFIN_FEATURE_FLAGS` lists only capabilities that still need a flag
rules.why: Functions and connectors are generally available since Rayfin 1.36, so `functions` and `connectors` in `RAYFIN_FEATURE_FLAGS` do nothing. Only `storage` still uses the flag.
rules.fix: Remove `functions` and `connectors` from `RAYFIN_FEATURE_FLAGS`, and the variable itself if nothing is left.

rules.title: Rayfin CLI is out of date
rules.summary: The Rayfin CLI is on the latest release
rules.why: Newer CLIs ship fixes and match the current documentation; behavior described on rayfin.ai may not apply to older versions.
rules.fix: Update `@microsoft/rayfin-cli` to the latest release — Fabricator can hand the upgrade to Copilot.

rules.title: Rayfin SDK is out of date
rules.summary: The Rayfin SDK packages are on the latest release
rules.why: The SDK and CLI version independently, and newer SDK releases carry fixes and the APIs the current docs describe. Rayfin 1.36 also changed several imports and Functions APIs.
rules.fix: Update all Rayfin SDK packages together to the same latest version — Fabricator can hand the upgrade to Copilot.

rules.title: Rayfin SDK packages are on different versions
rules.summary: The Rayfin SDK family is installed at one version
rules.why: `rayfin-core`, `-client`, `-data`, `-auth`, `-auth-provider-fabric`, `-lib`, `-functions`, `-storage`, `-embed-host`, and `-local-dev` ship in lockstep; mixing versions is untested and can break at runtime.
rules.fix: Pin every Rayfin SDK package to the same version (normally the latest) and reinstall.

rules.title: Connector package isn't pinned to the CLI's version
rules.summary: Connector packages are pinned to the version the CLI installs
rules.why: Connector packages ship in lockstep with the CLI, but their npm tags can lag behind. An unpinned install can pull an older connector that brings its own `rayfin-data`, leaving two Rayfin versions in one app.
rules.fix: Install the exact version `rayfin connector add` prints (normally the CLI's version), without `^` or `~`.

docs.title: Install connector packages at the pinned version

rules.title: Connector schema bundles decorated entity classes
rules.summary: Connector `schema.ts` files list entity fields by name unless relationship paths need the classes
rules.why: Importing entity classes as values ships their decorators into the browser bundle. The build and deploy succeed, but the deployed page can render blank.
rules.fix: In `rayfin/connectors/<name>/schema.ts`, list each entity's scalar fields as a string array in `connectorConfig.entities` and use `import type` / `export type` for the classes. Keep the class form only when the app selects relationship paths such as `orderItems.quantity`, and check that the deployed page loads.

docs.title: Decorated entity classes can break a browser bundle

rules.title: Semantic model or KQL connector uses application auth
rules.summary: Semantic model and KQL connectors use delegated auth
rules.why: `auth.type: application` isn't allowed for `fabric-semanticmodel` and `kusto` connectors, so `rayfin up` rejects the configuration.
rules.fix: Set `auth.type: delegated` for these connectors.

docs.title: Allowed auth values per connector type

rules.title: Connector folder has no rayfin.yml entry
rules.summary: Every `rayfin/connectors` folder matches a connector in rayfin.yml
rules.why: A leftover connector folder is no longer deployed or refreshed, but app code may still import from it.
rules.fix: Delete the folder and its imports, or re-add the connector with `rayfin connector add`.

rules.title: Connector isn't wired consistently
rules.summary: Connector names and runtimes match across rayfin.yml, schema, and client
rules.why: The connector key must be identical in rayfin.yml, the connector schema type, the client's `connectors` option, and — for semantic model and KQL connectors — the runtime map, or calls fail or return undecoded data.
rules.fix: Use one key everywhere, and pass the runtime map (`fabricSemanticModel()`, `kusto()`) as the client's second constructor argument.
rules.check: Cross-check connector names in rayfin.yml against the connector schema exports (for example AppConnectorsSchema), the ConnectorsRayfinClient connectors config, and the runtime map. Flag mismatches, and fabric-semanticmodel or kusto connectors without a runtime entry.

docs.title: Pass runtimes in the second argument

rules.title: `RayfinContext` is imported from the wrong package
rules.summary: Functions import `RayfinContext` and `AudienceType` from `@microsoft/fabric-user-data-functions`
rules.why: `RayfinContext` and `AudienceType` come from `@microsoft/fabric-user-data-functions`; importing them from `@microsoft/rayfin-functions` (the frontend client) fails.
rules.fix: Import them from `@microsoft/fabric-user-data-functions`.

rules.title: Function's SQL client has a known Fabric connection bug
rules.summary: Functions use `mssql@^12.6.0` with `encrypt: true`
rules.why: Older `mssql` versions pull in a `tedious` release with a login bug that causes "socket hang up" errors on Fabric SQL endpoints, and `encrypt: 'strict'` doesn't match what Fabric expects.
rules.fix: Use `mssql@^12.6.0` and `encrypt: true`.

rules.title: Function handler isn't registered
rules.summary: Every function handler is registered with `udf.func`
rules.why: Only handlers registered with `udf.func(...)` are deployed and typed for the client. `types.ts` is generated, so hand edits are overwritten.
rules.fix: Register each handler with `udf.func(name, handler, …)`, and regenerate types instead of editing `types.ts`.
rules.check: In the functions' source (rayfin/functions/, or the functions package rayfin.yml's services.functions.path names, such as packages/functions), find exported handlers that are never passed to udf.func, and manual edits to the generated types.ts.

rules.title: App uses experimental Rayfin Storage
rules.summary: Experimental Storage is noted for availability
rules.why: Storage is experimental: it isn't available in every Fabric region or tenant, and `@microsoft/rayfin-storage` may change substantially between releases.
rules.fix: Confirm a storage-enabled deploy succeeds in your target workspace before depending on it, and pin every Rayfin package to one exact version.

rules.title: Uses the deprecated Fabric callback bridge
rules.summary: No deprecated Fabric sign-in APIs are used
rules.why: `bridgeFabricCallback()` and the `callbackUrl` option only exist for older Fabric portals and will be removed.
rules.fix: Remove them and rely on the standard `ensureSignedInWithFabric` / `initEmbeddedAuth` flow.

rules.title: Rayfin agent files are missing
rules.summary: The CLI-managed Rayfin skill is installed for coding agents
rules.why: `.agents/skills/rayfin/SKILL.md` gives Copilot version-matched Rayfin guidance; without it the agent relies on older general knowledge.
rules.fix: Run `npx rayfin init ai-files install`.

rules.title: Import from a removed experimental path
rules.summary: Decorators come from `@microsoft/rayfin-core` and connector helpers from `@microsoft/rayfin-connectors`
rules.why: Since Rayfin 1.36, `@microsoft/rayfin-core/experimental` keeps only the storage `blob` helpers. Entity and field decorators, `RayfinPrimaryKey`, `Source`, and `AutoGenerated` were removed from it, so these imports break the build.
rules.fix: Import decorators and `RayfinPrimaryKey` from `@microsoft/rayfin-core`, and `Source` and `AutoGenerated` from `@microsoft/rayfin-connectors`.

rules.title: Connectors client comes from the old experimental entry
rules.summary: `ConnectorsRayfinClient` is imported from `@microsoft/rayfin-client`
rules.why: Since Rayfin 1.36 the connectors client is exported from the stable `@microsoft/rayfin-client` entry. The `/experimental` path still works for compatibility but is deprecated.
rules.fix: Write `import { ConnectorsRayfinClient } from '@microsoft/rayfin-client'`.

rules.title: Function uses a removed token audience
rules.summary: Functions use only the `Sql`, `Storage`, `Fabric`, `AzureAI`, and `ADO` audiences
rules.why: Rayfin 1.36 removed the `CosmosDB`, `KeyVault`, `EventGrid`, `Kusto`, and `WorkIQ` audiences, so code that references them no longer compiles.
rules.fix: Use one of the five remaining audiences, or store a key with `rayfin secret set` and read it as `ctx.Secrets.<NAME>`.

rules.title: Function uses deprecated `ctx.getToken()` or `ctx.getSecret()`
rules.summary: Functions read tokens as `ctx.Tokens.<Audience>` and secrets as `ctx.Secrets.<NAME>`
rules.why: Rayfin 1.36 replaced `ctx.getToken()` and `ctx.getSecret()` with the typed `ctx.Tokens` and `ctx.Secrets`. The old calls are deprecated and skip the checks on audiences and secret names.
rules.fix: Declare the audience in `RayfinContext<Schema, AudienceType.Sql>` and read `ctx.Tokens.Sql`; read secrets as `ctx.Secrets.API_KEY`.

rules.title: App uses Rayfin Functions
rules.summary: Functions availability in the target workspace is noted
rules.why: Functions are generally available since Rayfin 1.36, but not in every Fabric region or tenant.
rules.fix: Confirm a deploy with Functions succeeds in your target workspace before depending on them, and keep data access in `client.data` where a function isn't required.

docs.title: Functions are not available in every region or tenant

rules.title: Conflicts with current Rayfin guidance
rules.summary: The app follows the latest published Rayfin rules and known limitations
rules.why: Rayfin's rules for coding agents, known limitations, and deprecations change between releases, and the app may rely on behavior that is no longer recommended.
rules.fix: Follow the linked guidance for your installed Rayfin version.
rules.check: Fetch https://rayfin.ai/docs/reference/agent-rules.md, https://rayfin.ai/docs/reference/known-limitations.md and https://rayfin.ai/docs/reference/deprecations.md with web_fetch, and note each page's sdk_version. Report concrete violations in this app that no other listed rule covers, quoting the guidance and citing the page URL (with its #anchor) in docsUrl. If the pages can't be fetched, report this rule as skipped.

rules.title: Totals are computed by loading every row
rules.summary: Totals and summaries use server-side aggregation
rules.why: Fetching rows to sum, average, or count them in the browser is slow, uses capacity, and is capped by paging.
rules.fix: Use `.groupBy()` / `.aggregate()` and render the returned groups.
rules.check: Find code that loads lists and then reduces them (sum, average, min, max, count, group) for dashboards or totals where an aggregation would work. Don't flag small, bounded lists.

rules.title: Rayfin client is created repeatedly
rules.summary: One `RayfinClient` is created and reused
rules.why: Constructing a client inside components or per call repeats setup and can lose shared session state.
rules.fix: Create the client once in a module (such as `src/services/rayfinClient.ts`) and import it everywhere.
rules.check: Flag new RayfinClient(...) or new ConnectorsRayfinClient(...) inside React components, hook bodies without memoization, or functions called per request or per render.

rules.title: Page size is far larger than the view needs
rules.summary: Page sizes match what the UI shows
rules.why: Requesting thousands of rows per page (`.first(10000)`) defeats pagination and slows every load.
rules.fix: Match `.first(n)` to what the view shows and load more pages on demand.

rules.title: Very long list renders every row
rules.summary: Very long lists render incrementally
rules.why: Rendering hundreds or thousands of rows at once makes the page slow to load and scroll.
rules.fix: Show a page at a time with "Load more", or virtualize the list.
rules.check: Flag lists or tables that map hundreds or more rows (for example results of large .first(n) pages or merged pages) straight into DOM elements with no paging or virtualization.

rules.title: Heavy work runs on every render
rules.summary: Expensive computations are memoized or moved off the render path
rules.why: Sorting, filtering, or reshaping large arrays directly in a component body reruns on every render and makes the UI sluggish.
rules.fix: Wrap the computation in `useMemo`, or move it next to where the data loads.
rules.check: Flag obviously expensive work (sorting or filtering large arrays, heavy parsing, chart data shaping) done directly in the render body of frequently re-rendered components without useMemo, and data fetching started during render.

rules.title: Image has no alt text
rules.summary: Images have alt text (or `alt=""` when decorative)
rules.why: Screen readers can't describe an image without `alt` — they read the file name or skip its meaning entirely.
rules.fix: Add a short description, or `alt=""` for purely decorative images.

rules.title: Form control has no label
rules.summary: Inputs, selects, and text areas have an accessible label
rules.why: Without a label, screen-reader users hear an unnamed control and can't tell what to enter. Placeholders don't count as labels.
rules.fix: Associate a visible `<label htmlFor>` with the control, or add `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`.
rules.check: Flag input, select and textarea elements (and custom input components that render them) with no associated label element, wrapping label, aria-label or aria-labelledby — placeholder alone doesn't count.

rules.title: Clickable element can't be used with a keyboard
rules.summary: Clickable elements are buttons or links (or fully keyboard-accessible)
rules.why: A `div` or `span` with `onClick` can't be focused or activated from the keyboard and isn't announced as a button.
rules.fix: Use a `<button>` (or a link), or add `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, and an Enter/Space key handler.
rules.check: Flag elements such as div, span or li with onClick but no role, tabIndex and key handler, where a button or link would be the right element.

rules.title: Icon-only button has no accessible name
rules.summary: Icon-only buttons have an accessible name
rules.why: A button whose only content is an icon is announced as just "button", so screen-reader users can't tell what it does.
rules.fix: Add `aria-label` (for example `aria-label="Delete task"`) or visually hidden text.
rules.check: Flag button elements (or button components) whose only child is an icon or SVG and that have no aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or visually hidden text.

rules.title: Status is shown with color alone
rules.summary: Status and errors aren't conveyed by color alone
rules.why: People who can't distinguish the colors miss the status entirely.
rules.fix: Pair the color with text, an icon, or an accessible status message.
rules.check: Flag status, validation or error states where only the color changes (text or background), with no accompanying text, icon or role="alert" / aria-live message.
